newsitem.title: USA: Scattered showers improve Kansas crop conditions.
newsitem.headline: Scattered showers improve Kansas crop conditions.

text.p: Scattered showers improved Kansas crop conditions in the week ended Sunday and warmer temperatures allowed for planting of fall crops, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service weekly crop report said.

Wheat was rated eight percent excellent, 45 percent good, 33 percent fair, 11 percent poor and three percent very poor. The crop was 90 percent headed, compared with 86 percent both last year and for the five-year average.
Corn was 99 percent planted, in line with last year but ahead of the five-year average of 87 percent. Soybeans were 64 percent seeded, double the five-year average of 29 percent.
Corn was rated 10 percent excellent, 68 percent good, 21 percent fair, one percent poor and nil very poor.

"There are reports of Russian wheat aphids and greenbugs in wheat and cutworms in alfalfa with most of the infestations in the southwest," the report said. "Diseases reported are wheat streak mosaic, barley yellow dwarf and lead rust, with the southern third of the state reporting moderate damage."
Pasture was rated eight percent excellent, 61 percent good, 26 percent fair and five percent poor.
Topsoil moisture was six percent very short, 30 percent short, 61 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
